text:
Maya: quick idea dump 52u2014 instead of short soft leases, what if we use tentative writes + commit tokens for cross-region tolerant tenants. primary writes produce a `tentative-id` and local-read sees tentative but marked. remote can accept tentative and later commit/refine. reduces sync commit latency. thoughts?

Ravi: interesting. this sounds like optimistic multi-master but with explicit commit phase. big question: who decides commit? primary region only? that feels like a control-plane hitch.

Tom: we could attach a `X-Residency-Mode` header at request time: `mode=HARD|TENTATIVE|GLOBAL`. TENTATIVE -> allow cross-region but require `commit-token` propagation. HARD -> reject remote writes.

Maya: yep, commit authority model suggestion: ownerless but deterministic: commit when majority of shard replicas ack the tentative write OR after timeout the origin region commits. avoids control-plane involvement.

Ravi: for regulatory tenants HARD must be enforced by proxy at edge. no network rules should let tentatives out. we must integrate with KMS scoping: if residency != GLOBAL then do not export keys.

Tom: sample headers i'm prototyping:
```
X-Residency-Mode: TENTATIVE
X-Tentative-ID: tnt-20250615-778
X-Commit-After-Ack: 2
```

Maya: cache strategy: local cache serves tentative reads with `cache-tentative=true` header so clients can opt-out if they need only committed values. also add `X-Visibility: committed|tentative` in read responses.

policy-bot: policy alert: tenant=acme-eu, residency=HARD_LOCAL -> block outbound tentative writes. See policy id p-2025-07.

Ravi: rollback consideration 52u2014 how do we fast-repair if conflicting committed writes happen in different regions? vector-clock or last-writer-wins? prefer application-level merge for complex tenants; fallback LWW with tombstone versioning otherwise.

Tom: agree. also need a small reconciliation pipeline: consume tentatives from remote, attempt apply to primary, emit metrics if conflict resolution required. name: tentative-reconciler.

Maya: monitoring we need: tentative-created-rate, tentative-commit-latency, tentative-conflict-rate, tentative-abort-rate-by-tenant-policy. also tenant-level alarm if tentative-abort-rate > 0.1% for HARD_LOCAL misclassified tenants.

Ravi: ops concern: if many tentatives pile up during regional outage, backlog can hit storage. add TTL for tentatives (eg 2m) and a bounded queue plus backpressure header `X-Tentative-Backpressure: true` to tell proxies to rate-limit.

Tom: performance note 52u2014 tentatives add metadata per key. quantization plan: batch tentatives into single protobuf envelope for write-stream to reduce overhead.

Maya: canary plan: enable TENTATIVE mode for GLOBAL tenants only at 1% initially. will not touch SOFT/HARD. ops-bot schedule?

ops-bot: scheduled: tentative-write canary -> 2025-06-18T14:00:00Z for 1% GLOBAL traffic in us-west-2. channel #infra-metrics will get alerts.

Ravi: runbook items: how to force-commit or abort tentatives manually; how to quarantine tenant if tombstone conflict blasts. i'll draft emergency steps.

Tom: dev note: prefer data-plane implemention for tentative envelope handling, control-plane only for long-term policy changes. reduces p50 impact.

Maya: follow-ups: Tom will open proxy PR for headers + cache tagging, Ravi will draft runbook and policy checks, I'll wire reconciler job and metrics. will post results in this thread after canary. :thumbsup:
